sanskrit: tataḥ prahastaṃ niryāntaṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam garjantaṃ sumahākāyaṃ rākṣasair abhisaṃvṛtam
english: Then the great monkey army beheld Prahasta marching forth — terrible, of terrible valour, roaring, of immense body, surrounded by rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dadarśa mahatī senā vānarāṇāṃ balīyasām atisaṃjātaroṣāṇāṃ prahastam abhigarjatām
english: The mighty army of the most powerful monkeys, exceedingly enraged, saw Prahasta and roared back at him.

sanskrit: khaḍgaśaktyaṣṭibāṇāś ca śūlāni musalāni ca gadāś ca parighāḥ prāsā vividhāś ca paraśvadhāḥ
english: Swords, lances, staffs, arrows, spears, clubs, maces, iron bars, javelins, and axes of many kinds —

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi ca vicitrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ jayaiṣiṇām pragṛhītāny aśobhanta vānarān abhidhāvatām
english: — and variously adorned bows, all raised aloft by victory-seeking rākṣasas rushing at the monkeys, shone brilliantly.

sanskrit: jagṛhuḥ pādapāṃś cāpi puṣpitān vānararṣabhāḥ śilāś ca vipulā dīrghā yoddhukāmāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: The bull-like monkeys, eager to fight, seized flowering trees and broad, long boulders.

sanskrit: teṣām anyonyam āsādya saṃgrāmaḥ sumahān abhūt bahūnām aśmavṛṣṭiṃ ca śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca varṣatām
english: When the two sides met, a tremendous battle arose, with many warriors pouring down showers of stones and showers of arrows upon one another.

sanskrit: bahavo rākṣasā yuddhe bahūn vānarayūthapān vānarā rākṣasāṃś cāpi nijaghnur bahavo bahūn
english: Many rākṣasas in battle slew many monkey troop-leaders, and many monkeys likewise slew many rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śūlaiḥ pramathitāḥ ke cit ke cit tu paramāyudhaiḥ parighair āhatāḥ ke cit ke cic chinnāḥ paraśvadhaiḥ
english: Some were slaughtered by spears, some struck down by mighty weapons, some beaten with iron bars, and some hewn apart by axes.

sanskrit: nirucchvāsāḥ punaḥ ke cit patitā dharaṇītale vibhinnahṛdayāḥ ke cid iṣusaṃtānasaṃditāḥ
english: Some fell breathless upon the ground; some had their hearts cloven asunder; some were pierced through by a continuous stream of arrows.

sanskrit: ke cid dvidhākṛtāḥ khaḍgaiḥ sphurantaḥ patitā bhuvi vānarā rākṣasaiḥ śūlaiḥ pārśvataś ca vidāritāḥ
english: Some were split in two by swords and fell quivering upon the earth; monkeys were ripped open through the flanks by the spears of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vānaraiś cāpi saṃkruddhai rākṣasaughāḥ samantataḥ pādapair giriśṛṅgaiś ca saṃpiṣṭā vasudhātale
english: And by the enraged monkeys, great swarms of rākṣasas on all sides were crushed to the ground with trees and mountain peaks.

sanskrit: vajrasparśatalair hastair muṣṭibhiś ca hatā bhṛśam vemuḥ śoṇitam āsyebhyo viśīrṇadaśanekṣaṇaḥ
english: Struck hard with palms and fists that hit like thunderbolts, they cried out and vomited blood from their mouths, their teeth and eyes shattered.

sanskrit: ārtasvaraṃ ca svanatāṃ siṃhanādaṃ ca nardatām babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo harīṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ yudhi
english: Of the monkeys and rākṣasas in battle — some shrieking cries of pain, some roaring lion-roars — a tumultuous din arose.

sanskrit: vānarā rākṣasāḥ kruddhā vīramārgam anuvratāḥ vivṛttanayanāḥ krūrāś cakruḥ karmāṇy abhītavat
english: The furious monkeys and rākṣasas, devoted to the path of heroes, with eyes wide open, fierce, performed their deeds fearlessly.

sanskrit: narāntakaḥ kumbhahanur mahānādaḥ samunnataḥ ete prahastasacivāḥ sarve jaghnur vanaukasaḥ
english: Narāntaka, Kumbhahanu, and the towering Mahānāda — all these ministers of Prahasta struck down the forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śīghraṃ nighnatāṃ cāpi vānarān dvivido giriśṛṅgeṇa jaghānaikaṃ narāntakam
english: As they rushed forward swiftly and struck down the monkeys, Dvivida slew Narāntaka alone with a mountain peak.

sanskrit: durmukhaḥ punar utpāṭya kapiḥ sa vipuladrumam rākṣasaṃ kṣiprahastas tu samunnatam apothayat
english: Then the monkey Durmukha, quick of hand, uprooted a great tree and smashed the towering rākṣasa Mahānāda.

sanskrit: jāmbavāṃs tu susaṃkruddhaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ śilām pātayām āsa tejasvī mahānādasya vakṣasi
english: Then Jāmbavān, greatly enraged and full of brilliance, seized an enormous boulder and hurled it onto the chest of Mahānāda.

sanskrit: atha kumbhahanus tatra tāreṇāsādya vīryavān vṛkṣeṇābhihato mūrdhni prāṇāṃs tatyāja rākṣasaḥ
english: Then Kumbhahanu was encountered there by the valiant Tāra; struck on the head with a tree, the rākṣasa gave up his life.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇas tat karma prahasto ratham āsthitaḥ cakāra kadanaṃ ghoraṃ dhanuṣpāṇir vanaukasām
english: Prahasta, unable to endure this, mounted his chariot and, bow in hand, wrought terrible slaughter among the forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: āvarta iva saṃjajñe ubhayoḥ senayos tadā kṣubhitasyāprameyasya sāgarasyeva nisvanaḥ
english: Then between the two armies there arose what seemed like a whirlpool, and a sound like that of the immeasurable, churning ocean.

sanskrit: mahatā hi śaraugheṇa prahasto yuddhakovidaḥ ardayām āsa saṃkruddho vānarān paramāhave
english: For Prahasta, skilled in warfare and greatly wrathful, afflicted the monkeys with a great torrent of arrows in that supreme battle.

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ śarīrais tu rākṣasānāṃ ca medinī babhūva nicitā ghorā patitair iva parvataiḥ
english: The dreadful earth was heaped with the bodies of monkeys and rākṣasas, as if with fallen mountains.

sanskrit: sā mahīrudhiraugheṇa pracchannā saṃprakāśate saṃchannā mādhave māsi palāśair iva puṣpitaiḥ
english: That earth, covered by a great flood of blood, shone like the month of Mādhava covered with the blossoms of the palāśa tree.

sanskrit: hatavīraughavaprāṃ tu bhagnāyudhamahādrumām śoṇitaughamahātoyāṃ yamasāgaragāminīm
english: The embankments of that river were heaps of slain heroes; its great trees were shattered weapons; its great waters were floods of blood — a river flowing to the ocean of Yama —

sanskrit: yakṛtplīhamahāpaṅkāṃ vinikīrṇāntraśaivalām bhinnakāyaśiromīnām aṅgāvayavaśāḍvalām
english: — its great mud was made of livers and spleens; its aquatic moss was scattered entrails; its fish were severed bodies and heads; its grass was made of limbs and body-parts —

sanskrit: gṛdhrahaṃsagaṇākīrṇāṃ kaṅkasārasasevitām medhaḥphenasamākīrṇām ārtastanitanisvanām
english: — thronged with flocks of vultures and herons, frequented by kaṅka-birds and sārasas, covered with the foam of fat, resounding with cries of agony —

sanskrit: tāṃ kāpuruṣadustārāṃ yuddhabhūmimayīṃ nadīm nadīm iva ghanāpāye haṃsasārasasevitām
english: — that river formed of the battlefield, impossible for cowards to cross, like a river at the end of the rains frequented by swans and sārasas —

sanskrit: rākṣasāḥ kapimukhyāś ca terus tāṃ dustarāṃ nadīm yathā padmarajodhvastāṃ nalinīṃ gajayūthapāḥ
english: — that impassable river the rākṣasas and the leading monkeys crossed, as elephant herd-lords cross a lotus pool whose pollen has been scattered.

sanskrit: tataḥ sṛjantaṃ bāṇaughān prahastaṃ syandane sthitam dadarśa tarasā nīlo vinighnantaṃ plavaṃgamān
english: Then Nīla swiftly saw Prahasta standing in his chariot, releasing torrents of arrows and slaying the monkeys.

sanskrit: sa taṃ paramadurdharṣam āpatantaṃ mahākapiḥ prahastaṃ tāḍayām āsa vṛkṣam utpāṭya vīryavān
english: The mighty great monkey Nīla, valiant, uprooted a tree and struck Prahasta who was rushing toward him — utterly difficult to overcome.

sanskrit: sa tenābhihataḥ kruddho nadan rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi plavagānāṃ camūpatau
english: Struck by him, the enraged bull among rākṣasas, roaring, poured showers of arrows upon the commander of the monkey army.

sanskrit: apārayan vārayituṃ pratyagṛhṇān nimīlitaḥ yathaiva govṛṣo varṣaṃ śāradaṃ śīghram āgatam
english: Unable to ward it off, Nīla received it with eyes half-closed, as a bull-ox receives the autumn rain that has arrived swiftly.

sanskrit: evam eva prahastasya śaravarṣaṃ durāsadam nimīlitākṣaḥ sahasā nīlaḥ sehe sudāruṇam
english: In exactly this way, Nīla with eyes half-closed suddenly endured the fearsome, difficult-to-withstand shower of arrows from Prahasta.

sanskrit: roṣitaḥ śaravarṣeṇa sālena mahatā mahān prajaghāna hayān nīlaḥ prahastasya manojavān
english: Enraged by the shower of arrows, the great Nīla struck Prahasta's mind-swift horses with a great sāla tree.

sanskrit: vidhanus tu kṛtas tena prahasto vāhinīpatiḥ pragṛhya musalaṃ ghoraṃ syandanād avapupluve
english: Prahasta, the army commander, thus rendered bowless by him, seized a terrible club and leaped down from his chariot.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau vāhinīmukhyau jātaroṣau tarasvinau sthitau kṣatajadigdhāṅgau prabhinnāv iva kuñjarau
english: Both commanders of the armies, roused to wrath and swift, stood with bodies smeared with blood, like two maddened elephants.

sanskrit: ullikhantau sutīkṣṇābhir daṃṣṭrābhiḥ itaretaram siṃhaśārdūlasadṛśau siṃhaśārdūlaceṣṭitau
english: Raking each other with their very sharp tusks — those two resembling lions and tigers, moving like lions and tigers.

sanskrit: vikrāntavijayau vīrau samareṣv anivartinau kāṅkṣamāṇau yaśaḥ prāptuṃ vṛtravāsavayoḥ samau
english: Those two heroes, victorious in their prowess, never turning back in battle, eager to attain glory — equals of Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: ājaghāna tadā nīlaṃ lalāṭe musalena saḥ prahastaḥ paramāyastas tasya susrāva śoṇitam
english: Then Prahasta, greatly exerting himself, struck Nīla on the forehead with his club; blood flowed from that blow.

sanskrit: tataḥ śoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ pragṛhya sumahātarum prahastasyorasi kruddho visasarja mahākapiḥ
english: Then the great monkey, his body smeared with blood, furious, seized an enormous tree and hurled it at Prahasta's chest.

sanskrit: tam acintyaprahāraṃ sa pragṛhya musalaṃ mahat abhidudrāva balinaṃ balī nīlaṃ plavaṃgamam
english: He — Prahasta, himself powerful — seized his great club to strike an inconceivable blow and charged at the mighty monkey Nīla.

sanskrit: tam ugravegaṃ saṃrabdham āpatantaṃ mahākapiḥ tataḥ saṃprekṣya jagrāha mahāvego mahāśilām
english: Then the great monkey, himself of great speed, watching him — fierce and furious — as he rushed forward with terrible velocity, seized an enormous boulder.

sanskrit: tasya yuddhābhikāmasya mṛdhe musalayodhinaḥ prahastasya śilāṃ nīlo mūrdhni tūrṇam apātayat
english: Upon Prahasta — who was eager for battle, fighting with his club — Nīla swiftly brought the boulder crashing down upon his head.

sanskrit: sā tena kapimukhyena vimuktā mahatī śilā bibheda bahudhā ghorā prahastasya śiras tadā
english: That great, terrible boulder, released by the foremost of monkeys, shattered Prahasta's head into many pieces.

sanskrit: sa gatāsur gataśrīko gatasattvo gatendriyaḥ papāta sahasā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: He — his life gone, his glory gone, his vitality gone, his senses gone — suddenly fell to the earth like a tree with its roots cut.

sanskrit: vibhinnaśirasas tasya bahu susrāvaśoṇitam śarīrād api susrāva gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ yathā
english: From his shattered head blood flowed copiously; it flowed also from his body, like a mountain spring.

sanskrit: hate prahaste nīlena tad akampyaṃ mahad balam rakṣasām aprahṛṣṭānāṃ laṅkām abhijagāma ha
english: When Prahasta was slain by Nīla, that great, formerly immovable army of the rākṣasas, their joy gone, made its way back to Laṅkā.

sanskrit: na śekuḥ samavasthātuṃ nihate vāhinīpatau setubandhaṃ samāsādya viśīrṇaṃ salilaṃ yathā
english: They could not stand their ground once their army-commander was slain — like water that, upon reaching a broken dam, scatters away.

sanskrit: hate tasmiṃś camūmukhye rākṣasas te nirudyamāḥ rakṣaḥpatigṛhaṃ gatvā dhyānamūkatvam āgatāḥ
english: When that army-commander was slain, those rākṣasas, their effort spent, went to the dwelling of the rākṣasa-lord and fell into a mute silence of dejection.

sanskrit: tatas tu nīlo vijayī mahābalaḥ praśasyamānaḥ svakṛtena karmaṇā sametya rāmeṇa salakṣmaṇena prahṛṣṭarūpas tu babhūva yūthapaḥ
english: Then Nīla, victorious and of great strength, praised for the deed he had accomplished, rejoined Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, and the troop-lord was filled with joy.
